entries.content: AS004 is a derived analytical series measuring Marxian Productivity — productive output per unit of productive labor. This index captures the labor productivity of the productive sector as defined in the Shaikh-Tonak framework, distinct from conventional GDP-per-worker measures.
entries.source_ref: series_registry.json (AS004 definition: 'productive output per unit productive labor')
entries.verbatim_quote: H'p = h'p × L'p — Total hours of production and nonsupervisory workers in private nonagricultural sector. Where h'p = average hours per production/nonsupervisory worker (weekly); L'p = number of production/nonsupervisory workers (thousands). Source: BLS data for private nonagricultural sector. Example (1948): h'p = 40.00 hours/week; L'p = 34,489 thousand; H'p = 40.00 × 34,489 = 1,379,560 thousand weekly hours.

entries.content: Registry describes AS004 with description 'productive output per unit productive labor', source_type 'analytical'. The legacy construction script is A10_marxian_productivity.py. Units are index. The series covers 1948-2024. Status is 'book_period_partial_1948_1961', indicating only partial validation against the book for the 1948-1961 subperiod.
entries.verbatim_quote: Calculate average annual hours per productive worker: hp = (Hp/L'p) × 52. Example (1948): Hp = 974,250 thousand weekly hours; L'p = 34,489 thousand; hp = (974,250/34,489) × 52 = 28.24 × 52 = 2,079 hours/year.

entries.content: Marxian productivity = TP* / Lp (or a close variant), where TP* is Total Product of productive and trading sectors (S501) and Lp is productive employment (S515). As an index, it is likely rebased to a reference year. The distinction from conventional productivity is that both numerator (TP* excludes unproductive output) and denominator (Lp excludes unproductive employment) use the Marxian classification.
entries.verbatim_quote: Lp = L'p - (Lp)t - (Lp)fire. Where L'p = total production/nonsupervisory workers (from BLS); (Lp)t = productive labor in government (from Table F.1); (Lp)fire = productive labor in FIRE (from Table F.1). Example (1948): Lp = 34,489 - 8,629 - 1,496 = 24,364 thousand.

entries.content: Key inputs: S501 (Total Product TP*) and S515 (Productive Employment Lp). The construction array in the registry is empty, indicating this was handled by a standalone analytical script. The partial validation status suggests the book may only report this index for a limited period or that extension-period values diverge from expectations.
entries.verbatim_quote: Theoretical basis: Section 4.2 derives formula for relative rates of exploitation. Companion text: Section 4.2 (theoretical derivation of relative exploitation rates).

entries.content: Direct verbatim from Appendix J (chunk_36) defining the primary Marxian productivity measure q* = TPr/Hp. This is the canonical formula AS004 operationalizes: real total product per productive worker hour, with TP* drawn from Table E.2 and Hp from Table J.1 row 23 (= hp x Lp).
entries.verbatim_quote: Primary measure: q* (Total Product per Productive Hour). q* = TPr / Hp = (TP* / py) / Hp = Real total product per productive worker hour. Where: TP* = Marxian total product (from Table E.2); py = GNP price deflator (1982 = 100); TPr = Total product in 1982 dollars; Hp = Total hours worked by productive workers.

entries.content: Table J.1 row structure (chunk_36) showing AS004's index construction: row 2 defines the q* index as (q*/q*_1948) x 100, base year 1948 = 100. This resolves the 'Index base year not yet determined' known_issue.
entries.verbatim_quote: Row 1 | q* | TPr/Hp | 1982 $/hr by prod. workers. Row 2 | q* index | (q*/q*_1948) x 100 | 1948=100. Row 3 | TPr | TP*/py | billions of 1982 $. Row 4 | TP* | Table E.2 | billions of $. Row 5 | py | NIPA 704 1 | price deflator. Row 6 | Hp | see line 23 | millions. Row 23 | Hp | hp x Lp | millions. Row 24 | hp | Table I.1 | hours/prod. worker/year. Row 25 | Lp | Table F.1 | thousands.

entries.content: Page 140 (Table 5.14) salvaged-extract corroboration: q*/y captions Marxian-vs-orthodox productivity comparison; documents the central qualitative finding that Marxian productivity outpaces conventional measures, which is the explanatory purpose of AS004.
entries.verbatim_quote: q*/y: Productivity measures. ... Conventional productivity measure rises much slower than Marxian. Explains 'productivity growth slowdown'. Notes: a +1.2% per annum (1948-89). b +1.9% per annum (1972-82).

citations.full: Shaikh, Anwar, and E. Ahmet Tonak. 1994. Measuring the Wealth of Nations: The Political Economy of National Accounts. Cambridge University Press.

methodology_summary: Derived analytical index of Marxian productivity — productive output (TP*) per unit productive labor (Lp). Legacy script: A10_marxian_productivity.py. Only partially validated for 1948-1961.
